title: Workout of the Day
mechanic: Reading CSV files and printing tables

scenario.title: A plan made from a spreadsheet
scenario.body: The book's CSV files are tidy. Real ones come out of a spreadsheet with an invisible mark at the very start, spaces after the commas, a range typed backwards (50-20) and a row pasted twice. People also ask for more exercises than the list has. Every one of those should still give a sensible plan or a clear message, never a crash.

character.name: Coach Boing
character.role: a kangaroo who runs a very silly gym

tagline: Coach Boing picks today's exercises from a list and how many of each to do. Pick a lucky number, or write your own list of silly moves.

brain_blurbs.real: Also copes with messy lists from a spreadsheet.

rules.test_exists: Coach Boing is in the gym
rules.test_usage: Explains the workout when you ask for help
rules.test_bad_num: Won't plan zero or fewer exercises
rules.test_bad_file: Says so when the list file doesn't exist
rules.test_seed1: Lucky number 1 always gives the same 4 exercises
rules.test_seed1_easy: Easy mode does half the reps
rules.test_seed2_num8: Can plan 8 exercises from the full list
rules.test_seed4_num3_input2: Can read the silly exercise list too
rules.test_read_csv: Reads the good rows of a list and skips the broken ones
rules.test_too_many_exercises_is_a_clear_error: Ask for 20 exercises from a list of 9? He tells you nicely
rules.test_spreadsheet_byte_order_mark: Reads a list saved by a spreadsheet (it hides an invisible mark at the start)
rules.test_easy_never_means_zero: Easy mode never asks for zero of something
rules.test_no_exercise_twice: Never puts the same exercise in the plan twice
rules.test_empty_file_is_a_clear_error: An empty list gets a clear message
rules.test_table_lines_up_for_long_names: The table stays neat even with long names
rules.test_read_csv_forgives_a_messy_stream: "Hops" and "hops " are the same exercise, listed once
